threads.thread_goal: Align on pilot scope, roles and initial household targeting approach.

messages.text: Hi team, welcome to the channel for our Community Food Support and Outreach Pilot! I've attached the overview doc (A1) which covers our main goals. Let's use this thread to align on the scope and how we'll approach identifying the first households. Any initial thoughts?

Thanks for setting this up. I've read A1. To make sure we're all on the same page, what does success look like after 6 weeks? Is it about the number of parcels delivered, the quality of outreach notes, or just testing if the process works? Having a clear primary goal will help us make trade-offs later.

Good to be here. The scope in A1 seems clear. For T1, I think it's important we work with our community partners to define 'vulnerable'. It could mean many things - isolated seniors, families with young children, etc. That will affect what goes in the parcels.
Hello. I am ready to start. We can create a database for the households with unique IDs for tracking. I can set that up this afternoon.
Good question. I think success is about testing the process. So, did we manage to do it safely and consistently for 6 weeks? That's probably the main thing.

Okay, 'process viability' is a good focus. Let's add 'without any safety incidents' and 'positive initial feedback from >50% of households'. That gives us something concrete to measure. What do you think?
Yes, no safety incidents is the most important part for me.

That sounds great, much clearer. Let's formalize that. D1: The pilot's success criteria are 1) consistent weekly delivery for 6 weeks, 2) zero food safety incidents, and 3) positive feedback from over half the households.
For T1, we should use a numerical scoring system for vulnerability to be objective. We can assign points for different factors.

I'd be careful with a scoring system. Our partners usually work from established relationships and professional judgement. It's less about a score and more about who they know is struggling right now. Maybe we can start with a simple criteria like 'Referred by a partner organisation' and 'Not currently receiving other food support'.

I agree with keeping it simple. The referral basis is solid and respects our partners' expertise. How many households are we aiming for? The A1 doc doesn't specify. This will impact my route planning.
I was thinking maybe 20-30? Is that too many for a pilot?
From a food prep and packing side, 30 is manageable if we have enough lead time.

Let's start with a smaller cohort, maybe 15, for the first two weeks to iron out the logistics. We can scale to 25-30 for the remaining four weeks if everything is smooth. It's less risk of failed deliveries or food waste early on.
That phased approach makes a lot of sense. It also gives us a chance to get feedback from the first group before we expand.
Ok, 15 then 30. I will prepare the tracking sheet for 30 unique IDs.

Excellent suggestion. Let's go with that. So, to confirm D2: Eligibility will be based on partner referral and not receiving other food support. We'll start with ~15 households for the first two weeks, scaling to a max of 30 for the remainder of the pilot.
Great, we're aligned on scope and targeting. I will take the action to start the conversation with our community partners based on this. That's the first part of T1.

threads.thread_goal: Design and agree on the end-to-end operational flow from surplus collection to delivery.

messages.text: Hi all, let's start thinking about the operational flow. I've drafted a simple process for T2, the surplus food collection and sorting. The idea is: 1. Collect from stores at 8am. 2. Sort into categories (fresh, ambient, chilled) by 9am. 3. Log items and check dates. 4. Move to packing area. Any initial thoughts, especially from @429831 on feasibility and @516425 on timings?

Thanks. The sorting categories are good. We need to make sure we have separate containers for each and follow the Food Safety guide (A2). We should also have a 'reject' bin for anything that looks unsafe.

Thanks for this. From my side, I need to know when the packed parcels will be ready for collection. My delivery window is tight. If packing is done by, say, 11am, I can start my routes (T4) for an afternoon delivery run. Can we work towards that?

11am is a good target. That gives us about two hours for packing after sorting. I can start drafting the packing checklist for T6. It will probably include things like: 1 bread item, 3 veg, 2 fruit, 1 protein, etc. to ensure consistency.
The checklist should be a barcode scan system. Each item type gets a barcode. The packer scans them. The system confirms the parcel is complete. This eliminates errors.
This is great progress. How will we decide the delivery schedule? Is it one day a week?

Given my existing routes, I can dedicate Tuesday and Thursday afternoons to this pilot. We could split the households between those two days. That gives us a buffer if there's an issue on one day. I'll take T4 and map out two distinct routes.

A barcode system is a bit complex for our pilot, we don't have the equipment. A simple paper checklist (A3) that the packer signs should be enough for now, as per the project constraints. We can revisit for a larger rollout.
I agree, paper is fine. I can review the draft checklist (T6) when it's ready to make sure it includes a final check on packaging integrity and temperature for chilled items.
Fine. Paper it is.
Ok, so let's lock in these decisions. It sounds like we have a plan.

To summarise and confirm: 
D3: We approve the standard process: 8am collect, 9am sort (with safety checks), 9-11am pack using a paper checklist (A3), ready for dispatch at 11am. 
D4: Deliveries will occur on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons. I will own the route planning for T4. 
Does everyone agree?
Looks good. I'll finalize the process doc for T2 and draft the checklist for T6 based on this.

threads.thread_goal: Finalise safety, privacy and doorstep interaction guidelines.

messages.text: Hi team, following up on our process discussion, let's review the safety and interaction guides. I've asked @429831 to draft the Food Safety Quick Guide (A2) for T3, and I've put together a first draft of the Doorstep Script (A4) for T5. Please review and share your feedback.
Here is the draft for A2. It covers hand washing, temperature control, and checking dates. I think it has the main points. Let me know if anything is missing.
The guide looks like a good start. Should we add a line about cross-contamination, like keeping raw meat separate from other items if we ever get any?

Thanks for sharing the script draft (A4). I have a few thoughts from a delivery perspective. The question 'Are you in need of any other support?' is a bit too open and could put staff in a difficult position. Could we make it more specific, like 'We can also share a leaflet with contact numbers for other local support services, would that be helpful?' It's more manageable and still offers help.
The script should ask them to rate their wellbeing on a scale of 1 to 5. This will give us quantitative data to track over time.
That's a really helpful suggestion for the script. It keeps it non-clinical, which is a key constraint. I agree, let's change it to your proposed wording. Much better.

I don't think we can ask for a rating like that. It feels a bit too much like an assessment. The goal is a light-touch wellbeing check, not a survey. We need to keep the interaction brief and friendly.
Good point, I will add a section on preventing cross-contamination. Anything else?
Looks good otherwise. Simple and clear, which is what we need. Once that's added, I'm happy to approve it from my side.
Ok.

Great. So, let's finalize these. 
D5: We sign off on the Food Safety Guide (A2) with the added note on cross-contamination. @429831 can you upload the final version? 
D6: We agree on the final Doorstep Script (A4), using the 'offer a leaflet' wording suggested by @516425. I will update the document. 
Thanks for the excellent feedback everyone.
Will do. I'll update A2 and share it today.

threads.thread_goal: Set up tracking, labelling and logging tools before the dry run.

messages.text: For T7 and T8, I have created the templates for tracking and logging. See A5 and A6. For the labelling scheme, I propose a 6-digit alphanumeric code for each household, e.g., 4B32F1. This is fully anonymised and unique.

Thanks for drafting these. Looking at the log template A6, it seems to have a lot of columns. To keep it simple for the delivery team, could we maybe just have: Household Code, Date, Delivery Status (Success/Failed), and a small Notes field?

I agree with @44809 on simplifying A6. For the labelling code (T7), a random 6-digit code might be hard to read quickly when I'm trying to find the right parcel in the van. It's also hard to spot if one is missing from a sequence. Could we use something more structured? For example, TUE-R1-01 for Tuesday, Route 1, Stop 1. It's still anonymous but much easier to work with operationally.
I really like that structured code idea. It seems to meet the privacy needs while being practical. What does everyone else think?
A structured code is not truly random. But if it is required for operations, it is acceptable. I will update the documentation for T7.
The structured code makes sense to me. Easier to shout out if there's a problem, like 'Where is TUE-R1-01?' instead of a random number.
I will also simplify the log template A6 as requested.
Perfect. Let's make that the official decision then. D7: We will use a structured, non-random coding scheme for parcels and households, following the format DAY-ROUTE-STOP (e.g., TUE-R1-01).
Great, that will make things much smoother. Thanks @534740 for being flexible and updating the docs.

threads.thread_goal: Review dry run results and agree adjustments and next steps.

messages.text: Hi all, we've completed the one-week dry run (T10). From the operational side, things went mostly to plan. We had one issue where a batch of surplus bread was already stale on collection, which I've logged in A7. Packing took about 15 minutes longer than expected for the first batch.

Thanks for the summary. On the delivery side, the new labelling system worked perfectly. The routes were okay, but one street was closed, causing a 20-minute delay. I've also logged this in A7. The doorstep interactions felt good; the script was easy to use. Most people were just happy to get the parcel and didn't want to chat long.

The extra packing time is probably just a learning curve. We can probably speed that up next week. Regarding the stale bread, maybe we need to add a 'quality check' step right at the point of collection, not just during sorting.
I have processed the logs from A6. All 5 households were delivered successfully. There are 3 notes in the notes field. I have compiled them.
This is all really valuable feedback. It sounds like the core process works but needs a few tweaks. What does everyone think, are we ready to proceed with the full pilot next week?
Yes, adding a quality check at collection is a good idea. I can add that to the process doc.

I'd say yes, it's a 'go'. The issues we found are minor and fixable. My proposed adjustments are: 1. Add the quality check at collection point as @44809 suggested. 2. Build an extra 30 minutes of buffer time into my delivery routes to account for unexpected delays. With those changes, I'm confident we can scale up to the next group of households.
That sounds like a clear and sensible plan. Does anyone disagree with that assessment?
No, I agree. Let's go for it.
I am ready to continue.

Excellent. Then let's make it official. D8: We are 'go' for the full 6-week pilot roll-out, with two agreed process changes: 1) Add a quality check at food collection, and 2) Add a 30-minute buffer to delivery route timings.
I will now focus on the weekly monitoring for T11 and start thinking about the structure for the final report A8. Great work on the dry run, everyone!
